description: Verify order totals and largest-order selection through the library's public exports.
surface: a JavaScript library imported by Node consumers
isolation: Each command runs in its own process with in-memory order data.
baseline: Node 24 or later is on PATH.

launch.teardown: The import process exits on its own.

command: import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { total, largest } from './src/orders.js'; assert.equal(typeof total, 'function'); assert.equal(typeof largest, 'function')
doctor.asserts: Both public operations are available to a consumer.

drive.harness: Node assertions against public library exports
conventions: Run commands from the repo root.

standards: Keep each command's output and exit status in the proof record.

notes: Commands leave no persistent product state.

features.title: Order totals and selection
features.summary: A library consumer totals line prices and quantities and selects the order with the largest total.

subFeatures.description: Sum price times quantity for every line.
Select the order whose total is greatest.

entryPoints: Import total and largest from src/orders.js.

steps.label: Calculate totals and select an order
command: import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { total, largest } from './src/orders.js'; const orders = [{ id: 1, lines: [{ price: 5, quantity: 2 }] }, { id: 2, lines: [{ price: 3, quantity: 7 }, { price: 1, quantity: 1 }] }]; assert.equal(total(orders[0].lines), 10); assert.equal(total(orders[1].lines), 22); assert.equal(largest(orders).id, 2); console.log('totals 10 and 22; largest order 2')
steps.expect: Totals are 10 and 22, and order 2 is largest.

gotchas: largest expects a nonempty list of orders.
